_meta.description: Task 6 live-fire dual-send baseline — FortiBleed pivot slice
_meta.send_order: S3 first, then S4 (2s delay) — ensures EQL sequence order

wazuh.rule_132085_note: By design: if_matched_sid co-occurrence rule (rule-tree hangs off FortiGate chain, does not evaluate Windows json events, structurally cannot fire cross-source). Cross-source pivot correlation is handled by ELK EQL.
wazuh.rule_131021_note: S4 Windows JSON arrived in Wazuh archives (confirmed) but winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName not decoded without Winlogbeat agent — no decoder matches raw JSON-over-syslog. Rule did not fire.
wazuh.time_to_detect_132080_note: ~immediate; Wazuh @timestamp reflects log time; alert indexed within seconds of UDP 514 receipt

elk.eql_rule_name: FortiBleed pivot — SSL VPN valid-account login → AD account creation
elk.time_to_detect_eql_note: S3+S4 ingested at 13:40:21-13:40:23; EQL rule fired at 13:43:51. 210s = first scheduled 300s-interval run after ingest. Ingest latency itself was <2s.

real_ingest_path_notes: Both S3 and S4 transited filebeat (9514→filebeat→ES), were processed by auto-route + fortibleed-user-normalize, routed to vendor-specific indices (fortigate-* and windows-sec-*), and EQL sequence rule generated 3 signals with user.name=jchen. This validates the full production ingest path not covered by Task 5 (which injected directly into ES).
concerns: Wazuh S4 (4720 JSON-over-syslog): event arrived in Wazuh archives but no rule fired. Wazuh cannot decode Windows Security Event JSON without Winlogbeat agent — field winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName not extracted. This is a known architectural gap (see Task 4 findings: SAME_FIELD_VIABLE=false). Wazuh detection path for S4 is limited to EQL/ELK.

EQL rule produced 3 signals instead of 1. Likely because the windows-sec-2026.06.19 index contained 2 docs from prior test sends (both with user.name=jchen and event.code=4720). The 900s EQL window matched multiple S4 events against the single S3 event in the 15-minute maxspan. These are test residuals — a single FortiBleed pivot corresponds to a single S3→S4 pair; clean the index before re-running in production.

132085 (Wazuh if_matched_sid co-occurrence rule) confirmed 0 hits — by design: rule-tree hangs off FortiGate chain child, does not evaluate Windows json events, structurally cannot fire cross-source. This is not a CDB rule. Cross-source pivot correlation is the responsibility of ELK EQL.
